meta.what: THE TETHER DOMAIN, pilot: the Tether's rules as library entries the agent can read, so its method is a term it holds and not only code it runs (Isaiah 2026-11-13 10:38-10:44: 'codify the rules of the tether from each frame into NSM grammar/operators and provide templates'; 'how else can we claim true recursion'). Approved as a corpus import by Isaiah 10:44.
meta.run: AGENDA: a card is not lit by a reading. It is looked up by the SHAPE of what is unexplained (its when), and running it means asking its child questions (asks) in order. The agenda reader (item 2a, TETHER_AGENDA) runs them; the hand test (r1912) ran them by hand first.
meta.status: prior: inherited, protected from fading; its standing is still earned from the ground (LIBRARY_SPEC section 4: no head start for being given)
meta.grammar: library/grammar.json: operators + (and), ∥ (or), ≡ (same), → (then), ⇒ (implies), − (without), ⋛ (compare), ¬ (not); NSM primes SOMETHING, THIS, OTHER, PART, KIND, DO, HAPPEN, MOVE, BE, WHERE, WHEN, TOUCH, INSIDE, AND, NOT, IF, BECAUSE, THE SAME, MORE, LIKE, MAYBE, CAN

fields.when: the shape of the question this card applies to, in effect terms (never a cause)
fields.asks: the child questions, in order: the slots the Tether generates
fields.do: the rule as a molecule in the grammar's operators and NSM primes
fields.because: the figure line, verbatim, cited Fig N :line from docs/01-FOUNDATIONS/03-FIGURES_TEXT.md
fields.refuted_by: what reading on the board would show the rule failed here
fields.order: where it sits in the agenda (Fig 3: upstream first)
fields.do_sym: the same rule in the formula's symbols (grammar.json symbols), where a symbol exists

TETHER|Which link first.when: no progress: the goal's gap has not shrunk, or nothing is being tried
asks: SEE: can I tell what is in front of me, and tell it apart from what was there before?
WORDS: do I have a term for what this thing affords (moved, opened, joined, blocked)?
GOAL: can I say, in my own terms, what would count as progress here?
ROUTE: do I have a route to that, chosen under incomplete information?
KEEP: did I name what worked, verify it, and carry it?
TETHER|Which link first.do: (¬SEE ⇒ ask SEE) → (¬WORDS ⇒ ask WORDS) → (¬GOAL ⇒ ask GOAL) → (¬ROUTE ⇒ ask ROUTE) → (¬KEEP ⇒ ask KEEP); IF the first link NOT met is k THEN NOT DO work above k
because: Fig 3 :20 "The chain is ordered by dependency, not by importance. Each link consumes what the one above produces, so effort spent above the break arrives at a step"
Fig 3 :29 "Before asking whether a system is good, ask which link it currently stops at, and whether the answer was measured or assumed."
TETHER|Which link first.refuted_by: working on the first unmet link moves nothing, while work on a later link moves the goal's gap
TETHER|Which link first.do_sym: R⁺_s > 0 ∧ ¬shrinking(R_s) ⇒ ask the first unmet link

TETHER|Read the predecessor.when: a step never receives its input (a route never asked, a goal never formed)
asks: What step feeds this one, and did it produce anything?
TETHER|Read the predecessor.do: IF input(k) NOT HAPPEN ⇒ ask step(k−1) BECAUSE reading(k) = reading of nothing
because: Fig 3 :22 "A step whose input never arrives cannot be diagnosed, only its predecessor can. Which is why a reading taken below the break is not a weak"
Fig 3 :23 "reading. It is a reading of nothing."
TETHER|Read the predecessor.refuted_by: the predecessor's output is present and the step still fails, so the fault is in the step itself

TETHER|Instrument the middle.when: the agent has percepts and actions but no stated goal for this board, or a goal with no reading of progress
asks: What would an answer look like here? Write it down as a term, so it can be refuted like any other.
TETHER|Instrument the middle.do: IF ¬(GOAL has reading) ⇒ DO bind(THIS shape sought) → let it accrue a residual
because: Fig 3 :25 "Perception has obvious failures and obvious tests. Planning has obvious failures and obvious tests. The link between them, having terms for what a"
Fig 3 :27 "A link with no instrument is not a link that works. It is a link nobody has looked at."
TETHER|Instrument the middle.refuted_by: the committed goal shape's residual grows while play continues: the sought shape was wrong, refuse it and state another
TETHER|Instrument the middle.do_sym: ¬goal(s) ⇒ bind φ_sought as an ordinary term → let R accrue on it

TETHER|A state asks for its structure.when: a question about a STATE: where something is, when it changes, how much there is (space, time, energy)
asks: ORDERED HOW (spectrum): what ordering makes more and less sayable for it?
WHAT DRIVES IT (gradient): what difference, when spent, moves it, and which way?
WHAT IT RELATES TO (network): what is it connected to, and where does influence travel?
TETHER|A state asks for its structure.do: state(Q) ⇒ ask spectrum(Q) + ask gradient(Q) + ask network(Q); only those that TOUCH the residual
because: Fig 13 :29 "A state with no structure has no magnitude: three of what, ordered how, varying across what? A structure with no state is empty: an ordering over"
Fig 13 :28 "They alternate, and the alternation is where both the recursion and the randomness come from."
TETHER|A state asks for its structure.refuted_by: a child question answered and the parent state question no closer: that pairing did not bear on it here
examples: where the body is (space), how long it has been still (time), how many bar cells are left (energy): states
the reader tags a reading with symbols.kind_of_reading (o3.row -> state, space); a corridor is NOT a state, see 'A structure asks for its states' (the hand test's #9)

TETHER|A structure asks for its states.when: a question about a STRUCTURE: why things order this way, what drives a change, what is linked (spectrum, gradient, network)
asks: WHERE (space): near, far, between, contained?
WHEN, AFTER WHAT (time): in what succession does it change?
HOW MUCH, AT WHAT COST (energy): what is conserved or spent?
TETHER|A structure asks for its states.do: structure(Q) ⇒ ask space(Q) + ask time(Q) + ask energy(Q); only those that TOUCH the residual
because: Fig 13 :29-30 "A structure with no state is empty: an ordering over nothing, a network with nothing at the nodes."
Fig 13 :30-31 "So each step acts on one kind and yields the other, and every link in the chain is changed by the link before it. That alternation is the recursion."
TETHER|A structure asks for its states.refuted_by: as above: an answered child that brings the parent no closer
examples: a corridor or path of free cells, a group, what touches what (network); sizes ordered small to large (spectrum); a difference that pushes things one way (gradient): structures
'is the corridor wide enough' asks a structure for its states (space: near, far, between, contained?); the hand test's #9 asked it of a state and miscited the card

TETHER|Across the kinds only.when: a candidate answer joins two states directly or two structures directly
asks: What structure (or state) sits between these two?
TETHER|Across the kinds only.do: IF bond(state, state) ∥ bond(structure, structure) ⇒ ¬accept → ask the missing kind between them
because: Fig 13 :74 "Everything else is a composition across the two kinds, never within one."
Fig 13 :75 "Two states never bond directly. It is not space-time but space, a structure, time; and two structures join only through a state."
TETHER|Across the kinds only.refuted_by: a within-kind pairing that predicts the board and pays its bargain: a case the figure must answer

TETHER|Could it be reached at all.when: before searching any question, and before choosing a route on a board
asks: With the library as it stands, could an answer of this shape be reached at all?
On this board, can contact reach it: is there a press-and-watch whose effect would answer it?
Does the budget left (moves, bar cells, the slice's time) cover the route, before it is chosen?
TETHER|Could it be reached at all.do: ask reach(Q) ≡ closure(Γ) ∥ contact(the habitat) → IF ¬reach(Q) ⇒ answer(Q) = 'unreachable now' (a verdict, NOT a silence) → narrow; IF budget < route ⇒ narrow what is missing (more budget is a missing thing, said by its effect)
because: Fig 13 :132-133 "The second is decidability: given the library as it stands, could this have been reached at all. A system with a closure can answer that before it searches, and what it returns is a shape rather than a name."
Fig 13 :134 "So the system can report that it lacks something rather than producing an answer anyway. Unreachable is a verdict here, not a silence,"
Symbols table :107-110 "the habitat / the field of contact / Everything in contact with the residual: actors, conditions, relations. Enumerated, never composed."
TETHER|Could it be reached at all.refuted_by: an answer found for a question this card ruled unreachable: the reach check missed a route
TETHER|Could it be reached at all.v4_note: r1923 (c) + r1925 (g): never used in level 1, used late in level 2 (#41 missed, #46 first); at #86 reach -> no, on this bar -> narrow by effect ('more bar') found the refill at #88

TETHER|Narrow what is missing.when: a question ruled unreachable with the library as it stands
asks: Is this one question, or several that must be split first?
What is missing, said by its effect (what it would do), not by a name?
Then: mark it owed to an import before it is asked again.
TETHER|Narrow what is missing.do: unreachable(Q) ⇒ (ask split(Q) → ask effect(missing) → mark import owed)
because: Fig 13 :136-138 "What it can do is narrow. It can say the question is not one question and must be split before it is searched again. It can characterise what is missing in effect terms, which is the description that travels to a frame that may hold it. And it can say the answer is out of reach with the library as it stands, so something has to be imported before it is asked again."
TETHER|Narrow what is missing.refuted_by: a split whose parts are each reachable and still do not compose an answer: the split was wrong
TETHER|Narrow what is missing.do_sym: ∀φ ∈ closure(Γ): R|φ| ≈ R ⇒ split(R) → effect(R) → import owed

TETHER|Describe before you look.when: a new residual, before any lookup
asks: What happened, in effect terms: what changed, how many things, what is interchangeable, at what scale?
TETHER|Describe before you look.do: describe(R) by effect → THEN lookup(KIND of R); NOT lookup(name)
because: Fig 9 :27-28 "describe it before you go looking, or any frame you pick will seem to fit"
Fig 9 :45 "Describing the residual is the expensive part. Leaving, looking up and recognising are one step each, and cheap only in that order."
TETHER|Describe before you look.refuted_by: two residuals described the same that need different answers: the description missed a dimension
TETHER|Describe before you look.do_sym: describe(R_s) by effect → lookup KIND(R_s) in Γ

TETHER|Unbundle a union.when: one lever cleared part of a problem and the rest still binds
asks: Which two conditions overlap in what is left, and what does the overlap need of its own?
TETHER|Unbundle a union.do: IF lever(A) clears PART(R) AND R − PART ≠ nothing ⇒ ask overlap(A, B) as its own question
because: Fig 9 :54 "And when the split lands on a union rather than a partition, unbundle before you search again."
Fig 9 :57-58 "What remains is smaller and it is also categorically different: a case in two conditions is not a harder case of either. It stops being a mixture and becomes a specific compound."
TETHER|Unbundle a union.refuted_by: the remainder clears with a second single lever: it was a partition, not a union

TETHER|Filters for the budget, witnesses.when: a cut is about to decide an answer (a filter, a gate, a cheap screen)
asks: Is this a filter (spends budget) or a witness (the board deciding)?
TETHER|Filters for the budget, witnesses.do: filter ⇒ order candidates (ranked, reversible); ONLY witness ⇒ verdict
because: Fig 9 :60 "Use filters for the budget and witnesses for the verdict. Never let a filter hand you a verdict."
Fig 9 :40 "a wrong cut removes the answer and speeds up"
Fig 9 :41 "so keep every cut ranked and reversible"
TETHER|Filters for the budget, witnesses.refuted_by: an answer the filter removed turns out to be the one the board accepts: the cut was taken as a verdict
TETHER|Filters for the budget, witnesses.do_sym: filter: order φ by |φ| + |R|φ| ; verdict: the ground only

TETHER|Three texts before acting.figure: Isaiah's paper 'Decoding tacit knowledge' (adventuresinml, 2026), corroborated by Fig 9 and Fig 3
TETHER|Three texts before acting.when: before acting on an understanding of the board, and whenever an action did not do what it was for
asks: PRETEXT: what do I bring to this? Have I seen this kind before, and what does my record say happened?
CONTEXT: what surrounds it now? What is on the board and in contact with it?
SUBTEXT: what is it for? What would doing this get me toward my goal?
TETHER|Three texts before acting.do: IF ¬SUBTEXT ∧ PRETEXT ∧ CONTEXT ⇒ literalism → ask GOAL; IF ¬CONTEXT ∧ PRETEXT ∧ SUBTEXT ⇒ misapplication → ask what CONDITION here differs, and add it to the rule; IF ¬PRETEXT ∧ CONTEXT ∧ SUBTEXT ⇒ rote → ask WHY it worked before carrying it; IF only PRETEXT ⇒ projection → NOT DO, look at the board; IF only CONTEXT ⇒ noise → ask SEE and WORDS (Fig 3 links 1-2); IF only SUBTEXT ⇒ rumor → DO press-and-watch; IF none ⇒ nothing transfers → DO press-and-watch, transcribe
TETHER|Three texts before acting.do_sym: understanding ⇐ pretext(Γ, lineage) + context(o′, the habitat) + subtext(the goal's R)
because: Isaiah, 'Decoding tacit knowledge': "the way it gets rebuilt is contact."

Isaiah's table (11-13 11:09): pretext + context + subtext = understanding; without subtext, literalism; without context, misapplication; without pretext, rote; pretext only, projection; context only, noise; subtext only, rumor
Fig 9 :30 "your words are borrowed too, so describe the effect"
Fig 3 :10 "it can say what would count as progress here, in its own terms"
Isaiah 11-13 11:19-11:20: the table as the agent's failure guide; 'sounds good'
TETHER|Three texts before acting.refuted_by: an action taken with all three present that still does not do what it was for: the understanding was wrong, so a correction is owed
TETHER|Three texts before acting.source: Isaiah's corpus (his paper), not a figure; kept in this domain because it is a rule about how contact becomes understanding

learn_from_failure.misapplication: a CONDITION that limits the rule (the rule gains a scope, not only a lower weight)
learn_from_failure.rote: the REASON it worked (tier 1 -> tier 2 abstraction)
learn_from_failure.rumor: the situation and its history, by contact

readings_needed.pretext: does the record hold anything for this kind (tier-2 rules, settled terms, carried entries)?
readings_needed.context: do the conditions now match those the rule was learned under (its situation key)?
readings_needed.subtext: does this act serve a held goal (a goal hypothesis, an intent with a target)?

TETHER|Three texts before acting.caution: the record agreeing with itself is not proof (Fig 2; Isaiah's table: 'two experts drifting together, unchecked'); only the board decides

on_refuted.first: ask which text was thin; the block or the non-move itself is the reading
on_refuted.context: the board showed a condition the context reading missed: it becomes a SUBGOAL of the goal this action served (the goal needs it first), and the rule gains it as a condition (the hand test's #11 -> level 1's second goal; r1923 (b))
on_refuted.pretext: the record held nothing true for this kind here: press-and-watch, transcribe
on_refuted.subtext: the goal was wrong: refuse it and state another ('Instrument the middle')

TETHER|Could it have come out the other.when: before a reading carries a plan or a rule
asks: Could this reading have come out the other way? Which press or board would have shown the opposite?
If it reads the same in both cases (kept and restored, opened and not), what does it carry? Nothing: find a reading that differs.
TETHER|Could it have come out the other.do: IF reading(x) ≡ reading(¬x) ⇒ NOT carry; for a rule 'K opens after J changes': carry only IF J changed on some steps AND NOT on others, scored P(K | J changed) − P(K | ¬J changed) > 0, NOT by count alone
because: Fig 2 :29-30 "If it moves when you push on it, it is not an anchor."
Fig 9 :60 "Use filters for the budget and witnesses for the verdict. Never let a filter hand you a verdict."
TETHER|Could it have come out the other.refuted_by: a plan built on a reading that later proves uninformative (the hand test's #46 -> #121: 21 presses fell together), or a tier-2 rule whose contrast is 0
TETHER|Could it have come out the other.built_with: TETHER_TIER_CONTRAST (tether.py _tier_contrast, _tier_count): the tier-2 contrast check, as one test (tests/test_cards_v4.py)
TETHER|Could it have come out the other.source: the reviewer 2026-11-13, r1925 4 (e) + r1923 3; the hand test's #46 -> #121
